description: Compact seed histories for modern Latin letters.

letters.name: A
letters.origin: Often traced to Semitic aleph, associated with an ox/head sign, through Greek alpha.
letters.mutation: Rotated and abstracted from pictorial origins into a stable triangular capital.

letters.name: B
letters.origin: Traced to Semitic beth, usually glossed as house, through Greek beta.
letters.mutation: The house-like form became rounded in Greek and Latin writing.

letters.name: C
letters.origin: Latin C descends from a gamma-related form used by Etruscan and Latin scribes.
letters.mutation: Its sound history split: C first covered /g/ and /k/ before G was created.

letters.name: D
letters.origin: Traced to Semitic daleth, usually glossed as door, through Greek delta.
letters.mutation: A triangular delta line became the rounded Latin D.

letters.name: E
letters.origin: Traced to Semitic he through Greek epsilon.
letters.mutation: Greek vowel adaptation helped turn a consonantal Semitic sign into a vowel letter.

letters.name: F
letters.origin: Latin F is tied to waw/digamma pathways through Greek and Etruscan forms.
letters.mutation: A sign connected with /w/ became Latin /f/ through Etruscan adaptation.

letters.name: G
letters.origin: G was created in Latin as a modified C to distinguish /g/ from /k/.
letters.mutation: A stroke turned C into a new letter species.

letters.name: H
letters.origin: H descends through Greek eta/related forms, with sound values shifting across languages.
letters.mutation: A consonant sign became a vowel in some Greek dialects but remained H-like in Latin.

letters.name: I
letters.origin: Traced to Semitic yod through Greek iota.
letters.mutation: A small linear mark became both vowel I and, later, the ancestor of J.

letters.name: J
letters.origin: J is a later differentiated form of I.
letters.mutation: A swash or terminal variant of I became a separate letter.

letters.name: K
letters.origin: Traced to Semitic kaph through Greek kappa.
letters.mutation: Kept a recognizable angled skeleton while losing most pictorial meaning.

letters.name: L
letters.origin: Traced to Semitic lamed through Greek lambda.
letters.mutation: A more complex early sign became a simple right angle in Latin capitals.

letters.name: M
letters.origin: Traced to Semitic mem, usually associated with water, through Greek mu.
letters.mutation: Wave-like ancestry stabilized into angular strokes.

letters.name: N
letters.origin: Traced to Semitic nun through Greek nu.
letters.mutation: A serpentine/linear ancestor became a diagonal bridge between vertical stems.

letters.name: O
letters.origin: Traced to Semitic ayin, often glossed as eye, through Greek omicron.
letters.mutation: A pictorial eye became one of the most stable circular letters.

letters.name: P
letters.origin: Traced to Semitic pe through Greek pi.
letters.mutation: The form changed strongly across scripts before stabilizing as Latin P.

letters.name: Q
letters.origin: Traced to Semitic qoph through Greek qoppa and Italic use.
letters.mutation: A marginal Greek letter survived strongly in Latin as Q.

letters.name: R
letters.origin: Traced to Semitic resh through Greek rho.
letters.mutation: Latin added a leg to distinguish R from P-like forms.

letters.name: S
letters.origin: Latin S comes through Greek sigma, with deeper Semitic ancestry debated in details.
letters.mutation: Angular zigzags softened into the familiar curve.

letters.name: T
letters.origin: Traced to Semitic taw through Greek tau.
letters.mutation: A mark/cross sign became the simple vertical-and-bar capital.

letters.name: U
letters.origin: U differentiated from V much later in Latin-script history.
letters.mutation: A rounded variant separated vowel U from consonantal V.

letters.name: V
letters.origin: V belongs to the waw/upsilon family and originally covered vowel and consonant values.
letters.mutation: A single Latin V later split into U, V, and helped produce W.

letters.name: W
letters.origin: W is a later doubled form of V/U used for Germanic sounds.
letters.mutation: Two V forms fused into a new letter.

letters.name: X
letters.origin: X has a more tangled route through Greek and Italic letter values.
letters.mutation: A crossed form became fixed as Latin X with /ks/ value.

letters.name: Y
letters.origin: Y was borrowed into Latin from Greek upsilon for Greek loanwords.
letters.mutation: A Greek vowel sign became a Latin scholarly/import letter.

letters.name: Z
letters.origin: Z descends from zayin/zeta and was removed then later restored in Latin usage.
letters.mutation: A letter can go dormant in one alphabet and return through borrowing.
